planar_cop_judgement.what_the_worker_did: anterior axis = heel-to-toe projected into the leg plane; origin 100 mm along that planar axis from the ankle midpoint; lateral = plane normal outward; the 3-D heel-to-toe frame is retired
planar_cop_judgement.match_with_standard: Does not fully match. The standard (index.md, CoP frame, 23 Nov 2026) puts the origin 100 mm forward of the ankle centre along the foot's heel-to-toe direction, forward along the foot, up perpendicular to it, sideways outward. With toe-out the planar axis is not the heel-to-toe line, so the origin leaves the foot's own line, and the toe-out appears as a sideways shift of the whole frame. It is consistent only when the foot's heel-to-toe line lies in the leg plane. The new side-view-plane line ('CoP and foot frame follow the new foot plane') is ambiguous and can be read as the worker did.
planar_cop_judgement.evidence: Toe-out (heel-to-toe horizontal direction against the leg-plane forward) has median absolute values of 2 to 22 degrees by recording and leg (e.g. AB10 meander right 22, AB09 stairs left 20, AB13 normal_walk left 15), p95 higher. Distance between the planar origin and the 3-D heel-to-toe origin: median 0.4 to 3.6 cm, 95th percentile about 5 to 8 cm, maximum 9.4 cm (AB11 turn_and_step_1 right 9.5 cm, AB10 right 9.4 cm). Against the retired 3-D frame the planar CoP lateral coordinate moves outward by a median 1 to 2 cm (AB13 normal_walk left 0.5 to 2.5 cm median, right 0.0 to 1.1; AB05 left 0.3 to 1.8; AB10 meander left 0.3 to 2.4; AB03 right unchanged), while the anterior coordinate changes by only 0.0 to 0.5 cm. In the 3-D frame the lateral median was about 0.0 to 0.8 cm, i.e. the pressure point ran along the foot line; in the planar frame it carries the toe-out offset.
